title: Bacterio laminate, Abet Laminati product page
lede: The manufacturer’s current product page for Ettore Sottsass’s Bacterio laminate pattern.
summary: The Bacterio pattern in black on white: irregular squiggles and blobs at an even density.
made: Pattern 1978, per Abet’s and other sources; page current

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 25 September 2026 and inspected. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens. A cookie consent panel covers the lower half of the screenshot. The pattern is visible.

styles.note: The page calls Bacterio “the iconic pattern of the Memphis movement”. It shows the laminate that covered Memphis furniture surfaces.

observed: A large swatch shows the pattern: black squiggles, bars, and blobs of similar size spread evenly over white.
The heading reads “Bacterio | Ettore Sottsass” in heavy black sans-serif on a gray panel.
The text below says that Bacterio is the iconic pattern of the Memphis movement.
interpretation: The pattern that the [Memphis specimen](style:memphis) imitates with tiled squiggles. It is a real product, still in production, so it is the most direct source for Memphis surface pattern in this catalogue.
The page itself is not in the Memphis style, and the pattern is an image, so the fingerprint does not apply to this capture.
next: Record the pattern’s date from a primary source. The 1978 date comes from secondary sources and was not checked here.

images.alt: Abet Laminati product page: the heading Bacterio | Ettore Sottsass on a gray panel, a large swatch of black squiggles and blobs on white, and a cookie consent panel over the lower half.
